name: Cai ASB
question: Does treating asymptomatic bacteriuria prevent symptomatic recurrence in young women with recurrent urinary tract infection?

arms.label: No antibiotic treatment for asymptomatic bacteriuria
antibiotic treatment guided by urine-culture susceptibility

design.population: Sexually active women aged 18–40 years with recurrent symptomatic urinary tract infection and asymptomatic bacteriuria confirmed by the same uropathogen at at least 10^5 CFU/mL on two consecutive urine cultures.

verdictNote: No treatment yielded fewer symptomatic recurrences; the reported relative risk does not reconcile with the group risks.
takeaway: In young women with recurrent urinary tract infection, withholding antibiotics for asymptomatic bacteriuria led to fewer symptomatic recurrences at 12 months than susceptibility-guided antibiotic treatment (41/312 [13.1%] versus 169/361 [46.8%] among analyzed women).

reports.label: 12-month randomized report
reports.citation: Cai T, Mazzoli S, Mondaini N, et al. "The Role of Asymptomatic Bacteriuria in Young Women With Recurrent Urinary Tract Infections: To Treat or Not to Treat?" *Clin Infect Dis.* 2012;55(6):771-777. doi:10.1093/cid/cis534

results.measure: Symptomatic UTI recorded at the 12-month follow-up visit, divided by each group's initially analyzed size
results.note: Reported RR compares treated with untreated; it does not equal the crude ratio of the published analyzed-group risks.
results.locator: 2012 PDF p771, abstract Results; p775, Follow-up Results and Table 2

harms.label: Pyelonephritis during 12-month follow-up
harms.note: The article reports no significant between-group difference.

delivery.label: Bacteriuria and symptomatic UTI management
delivery.value: No antibiotic was given for asymptomatic bacteriuria in group A; group B received antibiotic therapy selected by antibiogram. Symptomatic UTIs in either group were cultured and treated by susceptibility.

delivery.label: Antibiotics used for asymptomatic bacteriuria
delivery.value: In the treated group, fosfomycin trometamol 31.4%, nitrofurantoin 26.8%, co-trimoxazole 19.8%, ciprofloxacin 13.1%, and levofloxacin 8.9% were used.
delivery.note: The paper reports percentages without drug-specific counts.
